post.description: Judged in the order sent, in one transaction; each change answers on its own, applied, conflict or rejected with a code. A patch applies only on the stored record's change tag; no base_tag creates. A change set (a genesis, rotation, approval, reset proposal or activation, team creation or team rotation) holds only its own key objects and applies whole or not at all: up to 10000 changes in one push, which still fits 4 MiB. A create of a key object equal to the stored one answers applied and writes nothing. Past grace or after a lapse a scope that exists takes key-object writes only.

tags.description:
TablePro Sync's record protocol (TablePro's ADRs 0051, 0052 and 0056). Every call takes the app's access token with scope app.

**Scopes.** personal, history or a team's TypeID. A scope exists from its first write; before it, the scopes list gives it a horizon of 0 and a pull an empty page with no cursor.

**Kinds.** Lowercase ASCII letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, with at most one . between two such parts, 1 to 64 bytes. Reserved, with the only scopes they go in: every key.* kind (personal, and key.version, key.wrap, key.ring and key.member in a team; key.member only in a team), secret_envelope (personal, team), history_entry (history only), library_connection, library_folder and library_query (team). Any other kind is ordinary in the personal and team scopes and needs no server release.

**Record ids.** Valid UTF-8 without U+0000, 1 to 255 UTF-16 code units, compared as bytes, never normalized or case-folded, in the form ADR 0052 gives the kind. No two team library ids of one kind may match once lower-cased, tombstones included.

**Fields.** At most 1 MiB once a patch applies, measured encoded without HTML escaping; at most 32 levels deep, the fields object itself being level 1 (so {"a": {"b": 1}} is 2 levels); no NUL anywhere; no JSON null stored (a null in a patch removes the member, RFC 7396). No key at any depth the secret rule refuses. A key kind's fields follow the body x-tablepro-fields-by-kind names: a duplicate, unknown, missing or wrongly typed member is bad_statement; bytes are canonical base64url without padding (RFC 4648 section 5), of the body's exact length and with zero pad bits; kind, start, av, signer_av, wrapper_av and kv are JSON integers with no fraction or exponent; no value the record id carries is repeated. Every key kind is create only. Two key objects are the same when their kind, record id and fields are equal as JSON values.

**Rejected codes**, per change; any other change of the push still answers on its own, except in a change set:
- bad_kind: the kind fails the syntax. bad_record_id: the id fails the syntax or its kind's form, but for a key kind's form, which is bad_statement. bad_value: deeper than 32 levels, or a NUL. secret_key: a key the secret rule refuses. too_large: over 1 MiB once the patch applies.
- kind_not_in_scope: a reserved kind outside its scopes. role: the caller's role does not write the kind or this team key object. policy: an install or team switch turns the kind off.
- create_only: a patch of a history_entry other than a revival over a policy tombstone; a patch or delete of a key kind; a create of a key kind where a different object is stored.
- writer_bound: a key kind whose writer its binding does not admit. request_pending: a second open key.request from one device row. request_closed: a key.sas step or approval the session does not take now, or for a request the server no longer holds. reset_held: a reset's activation before its held_until.
- key_dependency: a team version record or wrap naming an account with no key.member at that av. change_set: another change of the same change set was rejected. team_full: a confirming wrap that would give a 5,001st member the team key. id_case_collision: a team library create whose id matches another of its kind once lower-cased.
- bad_statement: a key object that fails the server's checks (ADR 0056, What the server stores and checks), its id off its kind's form included. key_version_stale and key_version_unknown: kv below or above the scope key's current version. rotation_due: a team secret_envelope while the team is rotation_due. quota_exceeded: a create past the scope's quota; none today.

**Change sets.** A genesis, a rotation, an approval, a reset proposal and a reset activation in the personal scope, and a team creation and a team rotation, each go up as one push holding only their own key objects, of up to 10,000 changes. The server applies one whole or not at all, and a pull never ends a page inside one. Any other push holds 1 to 500 changes, each record named once.

**Idempotency.** Every push carries Idempotency-Key, 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a new UUIDv4 per batch, kept under the account, the scope and the key with the SHA-256 of the body for idempotency_retention seconds. Every request, a replay too, is authenticated and checked for its DPoP proof, the gates and the role before a stored answer is looked up. A push that applied a change stores the outcomes of the changes that applied, in the transaction that wrote them; a replay with the same body answers those again and judges the other changes again, so one that conflicted may now apply. A push that applied nothing stores nothing. Another body under the key is idempotency_mismatch; a replay while the first runs is idempotency_in_progress. A batch older than the retention is pulled against and pushed again under a new key.

**DPoP.** Every call on the personal and history scopes, every write of a key kind or a secret_envelope, DELETE /sync/key-device and the stopped operations carry a DPoP proof (RFC 9449 section 4.2) beside the bearer token, which stays a bearer token. Header: typ dpop+jwt, alg Ed25519 (RFC 9864 section 2.2; EdDSA and every other value refused), jwk {"kty": "OKP", "crv": "Ed25519", "x": the DSK} with no private member. Claims: jti, 16 random bytes in base64url; htm; htu, the request URI without query or fragment; iat in seconds, at most 300 seconds old and 60 ahead; ath, the base64url SHA-256 of the access token; nonce once the server sent DPoP-Nonce. A repeated jti is refused. On clock skew the server answers use_dpop_nonce with a DPoP-Nonce; any other failure is device_not_approved. The proof's key: the DSK of the key device the token's device row holds, certified at the account's current av, for an approved device; the request's DSK for a key.request and its reveal and cancel steps; the approving device's for a nonce step, its cancel and the approval change set; the change set's key.device DSK for a genesis, and for a rotation from a device that is not approved; the DSK the key.reset names for a reset proposal and its activation; any key of a device of the account for a key.cancel the identity key signs; any valid proof for DELETE /sync/key-device and for reads before approval.

**Before approval** a device reads only the key kinds of the personal scope, and writes only its key.request and that request's reveal and cancel steps, a genesis while the account has no key.account, a rotation change set whose key.account the identity key signs, a reset proposal and its activation, and a key.cancel the identity key signs. Anything else is device_not_approved, the history scope included. Its cursors answer cursor_expired once it is approved.

**Step-up** (RFC 9470). A kind 3 reset proposal, and a device row removal from the apps (DELETE /devices/{device_id} for an account with keys), on a token with no fresh step-up answer 401 step_up_required with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", acr_values and max_age=300. acr_values is "urn:tablepro:acr:passkey" on a self-hosted install and "urn:tablepro:acr:passkey urn:tablepro:acr:email-code" on the SaaS. The app opens the authorization endpoint with those acr_values, max_age=300 and PKCE, takes the new tokens and retries. Fresh is an acr the challenge named and an auth_time at most 300 seconds old; a refresh keeps auth_time.

**A license key token** (a legacy key exchange) never reaches the personal or history scope and writes no key object or envelope: interactive_sign_in_required.

**Past grace or after a lapse** a scope that exists answers pulls and takes key-object writes, DELETE /sync/key-device and the stopped operations; a push holding any other change is license_expired past a self-hosted install's grace, feature_required after a SaaS lapse.

**Rate limits.** 120 requests a minute per sign-in and 600 per account over all of /v2; 429 carries Retry-After. Back off exponentially with jitter on 429 and 503.
